title: FinFET Inspection - Overlay Shift Detection on Puma 9900
subtitle: Incoming Wafer QC Quality Validation for 3nm Node Manufacturing
author: Maria Gonzalez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Puma 9900 system to detect and classify Overlay Shift defects during incoming wafer qc inspection at the 3nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 12 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Overlay Shift defects that are critical to yield at the 3nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Puma 9900 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Puma 9900
- Inspection Type: FinFET Inspection
- Target Defect: Overlay Shift
- Process Step: Incoming Wafer QC
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 3nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 12

This test case applies to all Puma 9900 systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 12 for incoming wafer qc monitoring in the 3nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Puma 9900
Software Version: v15.6.481
Recipe: FINFET_INSPECTION_3nm_INCOMING WAFER QC
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Low (130 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: 21-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Puma 9900 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'FinFET Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Overlay Shift defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 3nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 66 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 92% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.4% for FinFET Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.94 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-01-03
Wafers Tested: 7
Total Defects Found: 1265
Defect Density: 402.66 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 2.6%
Capture Rate: 85.3%
Test Duration: 135 minutes
System Uptime: 98.7%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Puma 9900 demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Overlay Shift at the 3nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Minor calibration drift was detected after extended run; re-calibration resolved the issue.

e) SECS/GEM communication was verified with zero packet loss during data transfer.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
